- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.53) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce the forecast peak to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.27) and forecast is trending up, cap the upward slope to prevent overcorrection.  
- After a recent spike in price, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast by 5–10% in the next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is high (≥ 0.80) and forecast is below recent 10-day average, adjust upward to align with sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is low (≤ 0.27) and forecast is above recent 10-day average, reduce forecast to avoid mean reversion bias.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below forecast, apply a downward bias correction of 2–5% for next forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes followed by recovery, model tends to overcorrect — dampen forecast slope after such events.
